**Anthony Albanese and the Labor Party**
Albanese led the center-left Australian Labor Party to victory over the Liberal-National Coalition in the 2022 election and became prime minister, governing from the capital, Canberra. He was re-elected in a landslide in 2025.

**Liberal-National Coalition**
The long-standing alliance of Australia's center-right Liberal Party and the rural-based National Party, which is the main rival to Labor. It governed under prime ministers such as John Howard, Malcolm Turnbull, and Scott Morrison.

**Scott Morrison and the "quiet Australians"**
The Liberal prime minister from 2018 to 2022. After his surprise 2019 election win, he declared that "the quiet Australians" had won a great victory, and he lost power to Albanese in 2022.

**2019–2020 bushfires and the Hawaii vacation**
The catastrophic "Black Summer" wildfires burned huge areas of Australia and killed vast numbers of animals, including kangaroos and koalas. Morrison was heavily criticized for vacationing in Hawaii during the crisis, and lingering smoke disrupted the Australian Open tennis tournament in Melbourne.

**Offshore detention on Nauru and Manus Island**
Australia sent asylum seekers who arrived by boat to detention centers on the island nation of Nauru and on Manus Island in Papua New Guinea. The Guardian published a database of leaked reports of abuse at the Nauru center, and the Manus arrangement was wound down by 2019.

**One Nation and Pauline Hanson**
One Nation is a far-right, anti-immigration party led by Pauline Hanson. When Hanson returned to the Senate in 2016, Labor senator Sam Dastyari sarcastically invited her to share a "halal snack pack," a popular kebab-shop dish.

**Malcolm Turnbull and the Trump phone call**
The Liberal prime minister from 2015 to 2018. In a tense February 2017 phone call, he pushed Donald Trump to honor an Obama-era deal for the U.S. to resettle refugees held in Australia's offshore centers, and his government also tried to change the words "insult" and "offend" in Section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act.

**John Howard and the AWB scandal**
Howard was the Liberal prime minister from 1996 to 2007. In 2006 his government faced a scandal after the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), Iraq's largest food supplier under the UN oil-for-food program, was found to have paid illegal kickbacks to Saddam Hussein's regime; his Labor opponent at the 2004 election was Mark Latham.

**2025 election and teal independents**
In the 2025 election, Labor greatly increased its majority while the Coalition suffered heavy losses, partly after reversing a policy to end work from home for public servants. "Teal" independents, socially liberal candidates focused on climate action, kept their seats, Clive Palmer's right-wing Trumpet of Patriots party flopped, and veteran election analyst Antony Green retired from broadcasting afterward.

**Novak Djokovic's deportation**
In January 2022, the Serbian tennis star was deported before the Australian Open because he was not vaccinated against COVID-19, after a legal battle over his visa.

**Penny Wong**
Albanese's foreign minister. At a Pacific Islands Forum meeting in Fiji in 2022, she promised that Australia would "end the climate wars" and help make the "Pacific family" even stronger.

**Harold Holt and "All the way with LBJ"**
The Liberal prime minister who expanded Australia's role in the Vietnam War, pledging in 1966 to go "all the way with LBJ" in support of U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson. In December 1967, he disappeared while swimming at Cheviot Beach in Victoria, and his body was never found.

**Kevin Rudd and the Stolen Generations apology**
In 2008, Labor prime minister Kevin Rudd formally apologized to the Stolen Generations, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children who had been removed from their families under government policies.

**Edmund Barton and the Hopetoun Blunder**
Barton was Australia's first prime minister when the federation formed in 1901. He took office after the "Hopetoun Blunder," in which the first Governor-General, Lord Hopetoun, first invited William Lyne instead of Barton to form a government, but Lyne could not get enough support.

**Robert Menzies and "The Forgotten People"**
Menzies founded the modern Liberal Party and is Australia's longest-serving prime minister. In a 1942 radio speech called "The Forgotten People," he praised the middle class as the backbone of the nation.
